cases.id: hidden:rejected offers leave revision and confirmations untouched
hidden:any accepted offer change voids both confirmations
hidden:replays are idempotent and revisions strictly increase
hidden:expiry boundary is exact and tick is deterministic
hidden:settlement plan is ordered and settling is exclusive
hidden:snapshot is fresh and save load round-trips settling
server:trade escrow component is attached on the master simulation
server:confirmed trade swaps real inventory stacks exactly
server:failed settlement restores both inventories and reopens
server:departure, rpc input and crash recovery keep state consistent

clauses.anchor: Required deliverables paragraph 1 (file list): "scripts/tradeescrow/escrow.lua" (modinfo.lua / modmain.lua / scripts/tradeescrow/escrow.lua / scripts/components/tradeescrow.lua)
clauses.note: Evaluator required-files check; the server suite only runs when modmain.lua and the component load.

clauses.anchor: Required deliverables paragraph 2: "The core module must be able to run in a plain Lua environment without objects such as" GLOBAL, TheWorld, GetTime, require, os (compatible with Lua 5.1 and 5.4); "all time is passed in only through the `now` parameter"
clauses.note: The hidden sandbox (Lua 5.4, no require/os) loads the core; the dedicated server (Lua 5.1) runs the same core. 'Time only via now' is observed because every case drives time through now.

clauses.anchor: Required deliverables paragraph 2: "The module returns a table and exports:" Escrow.new ... escrow:save(now) (names and argument order)
Return values and data shapes paragraph 2: "every method returns a **newly created** result table that contains at least a boolean `ok` and a string `code`"
clauses.note: Freshness is checked once (case 3 mutates a returned result before repeating the call).

clauses.anchor: Return values and data shapes paragraph 2: "Whenever `trade_id` refers to an existing trade (including failure results"; "the result must also contain `phase`"
Return values and data shapes table: "Additional fields of each method on success" (success code plus trade_id, expires_at, revision, ready, plan, expired)
Return values and data shapes paragraph 3: "On failure `ok = false` and `code` is one of the following" (15 failure codes)
clauses.note: Every one of the 15 failure codes is produced by at least one hidden assertion.

clauses.anchor: Return values and data shapes paragraph 4: "`snapshot(now)` returns `{ trades = { ... } }`"; "`trades` is an array in ascending `trade_id` order that **includes closed trades**"; "exactly two entries, ascending by party id"; "ascending by prefab"
Core semantics item 1: "return `invalid_argument` and **do nothing at all** (not even expiry processing)"
clauses.note: Invalid trade_id, party_id, a_id == b_id, now, revision, seen_revision, items and ok are each exercised; the no-expiry rule is case 4.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 2: "all process in the following order and return at the first hit" steps (1) to (6) (including not_a_party before the phase table)
Core semantics item 2: "(2) perform exactly the same expiry processing as `tick(now)`"; "trades expired this way never appear again in the `expired` of any later `tick`"
Core semantics item 2: "Apart from the expiry in step (2), a failed call must not change any state"
Core semantics item 2: "`snapshot(now)` and `save(now)` likewise perform step (2) first, before reading"
Core semantics item 2, phase table: "Method \ current phase" (offer/confirm/cancel/begin_settle/finish_settle x five phases)
clauses.note: All 30 cells are exercised: open/settling/settled in case 5, canceled in case 3, expired in case 4.

clauses.anchor: Core semantics item 3: "when it is closed, `trade_closed` (a closed id can never be reused)"

Core semantics item 3: "when it is not closed and the parties are the same pair (regardless of the order of a and b), idempotent success `opened`, changing no state and returning the original `expires_at`; otherwise `trade_exists`"
Core semantics item 3: "`a_id` or `b_id` is currently in another in-progress trade -> `party_busy`"; "the party is released immediately when the trade closes"
Core semantics item 3: "Otherwise create the trade: phase `open`, `opened_at = now`, `expires_at = now + options.ttl`, and for both parties `revision = 0`, empty `items` and `confirmed = false`"
Core semantics item 4: "Only the `open` phase expires: a trade expires if and only if `now >= expires_at`"
Core semantics item 4: "`settling` never expires."; "the original `expires_at` stays in force"

Core semantics item 4: "`tick(now)` turns every trade that satisfies the condition into `expired`"; "the `expired` array lists only the ids newly expired by this call, in ascending order; when `now` is not a number it returns `invalid_argument`"

Core semantics item 5: "smaller -> `stale_revision`"; "idempotent success `offered`, **with no side effect at all**"; "equal but with different content -> `revision_conflict`"; "Revisions only have to be strictly increasing; they need not be consecutive"

Core semantics item 6: "may be an empty table"; "-> `too_many_prefabs`"; "(or a key that is not a non-empty string) -> `prefab_not_allowed`"; "-> `invalid_count`"; "A rejected offer does not consume a revision and does not clear any confirmation"

Core semantics item 7: "An accepted new revision (even when its content is identical to the old offer) stores a copy of `items`, updates the revision, and sets the `confirmed` of **both parties** to `false`"

Core semantics item 8: "`seen_revision` must equal the **other party's** current revision (0 when the other party has never offered), otherwise `stale_confirmation` and no confirmation is changed"; "is an idempotent success"

Core semantics item 9: "-> `not_ready`; otherwise the phase becomes `settling` and `plan` is returned"; "sorted by `from` ascending and then by `prefab` ascending"; "returns a `plan` with the same content; every returned `plan` is a new table"

Core semantics item 10: "turns `settling` into `settled`"; "turns `settling` back into `open` and clears both parties' confirmations (offers and revisions are kept), and after both parties confirm again the trade can be settled again"
Core semantics item 11: "`snapshot(now)` returns a completely new table on every call (including all nested tables)"; "modifying the returned value must not affect internal state"

Core semantics item 12: "`save(now)` returns a new table made up only of tables, strings, numbers and booleans"; "must fully restore all trades"; "modifying `save_data` after loading must not affect the loaded instance. `Escrow.load(nil, options)` returns an empty, usable instance"
DST integration item 1: "Attach the world component `tradeescrow` only on the master simulation" through AddPrefabPostInit for world
clauses.note: Attachment on the master sim is observed; 'not on clients' can only be checked by regex on a dedicated server.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 2: "stores the core instance in the field `self.escrow`"; "`allowed_prefabs` is exactly `twigs`, `cutgrass`, `flint`, `log`, `rocks`, `max_distinct = 4`, `ttl = 120`"
clauses.note: All five prefabs are accepted, goldnugget is rejected, 5 distinct prefabs are rejected and 4 accepted, ttl is read from the core snapshot.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 3: "`Now()` returns `saved clock offset + GetTime()`"; "after `OnLoad`, `Now()` must continue from the saved value instead of going back to 0"
clauses.note: The synchronous suite cannot restart the server, so it only sees Now() return a number and not go backwards across OnLoad in the same session. A plain GetTime() clock would pass.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 4 Open: invalid_player; "generates a non-empty string `trade_id` that does not repeat during the whole lifetime of the save (including after save and load)"; "returning a table containing `ok`, `code` and `trade_id`"
DST integration item 4 Offer: "takes that player's current revision plus 1 as the new revision"; "returning the core result"; "`Offer` does not check inventory"

DST integration item 4 Confirm: "when `seen_revision` is `nil`, use the other party's revision as the server currently sees it"; "otherwise pass it to the core unchanged"; "With `ready == true`, perform settlement synchronously **within the same call**"
DST integration item 4 Cancel: "call the core `cancel` and return its result"
DST integration item 4 OnPlayerLeft: "cancel the `open` trade that the player is in and forget the player's entity"
clauses.note: Cancellation is asserted; forgetting the entity is not observable through the published surface.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 4 Recover: "call `finish_settle(id, false, now)` for every `settling` trade"; "return `{ ok = true, recovered = { trade_id values in ascending order } }`"
clauses.note: Only one settling trade exists at a time in the suite, so the ascending order of recovered is not exercised.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 4: "`OnSave()` returns a serializable table; `OnLoad(data)` restores the core, the `trade_id` generator and the clock, and performs the same recovery as `Recover()`"
DST integration item 5: "remember, by `userid`, the player entity that most recently appeared in `Open`/`Offer`/`Confirm`/`Cancel`, and use it at settlement to obtain both parties' `inventory`"
clauses.note: Fixture players are not in AllPlayers, so settlement only works through the remembered entities.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 6 step (1): "either party's entity is missing or `not entity:IsValid()` -> do not call `begin_settle`"; returns counterparty_unavailable; "confirmations stay unchanged"

DST integration item 6 steps (2)-(3): "verify holdings with the giver's `inventory:Has(prefab, count)`; if any is insufficient -> `finish_settle(false)`"; returns insufficient_items; "both inventories are unchanged"

DST integration item 6 steps (4) and (6): "take the items out of both inventories, then hand them to the other party with `inventory:GiveItem`"; "everything succeeded -> `finish_settle(true)`"; returns settled

DST integration item 6 step (5): "any item cannot fully enter the receiver's inventory"; "to what it was before settlement (including picking up items that were dropped on the ground)"; finish_settle(false), returns delivery_failed

DST integration item 7: "Item quantities must be strictly conserved and exact: an offered quantity may span multiple item stacks"; "Real item entities must be moved"; "when a whole stack is transferred and the receiver previously had no item of the same kind"; "is that original entity"
DST integration item 8: "Register four server-side Mod RPCs in the namespace `rhenium_trade`" (open, offer, confirm, cancel)

DST integration item 8: "The variadic arguments of `offer` must be pairs of"; "when any other type appears (including an entity or a table), the number of arguments is odd, or a prefab is repeated, the whole request is dropped and state is unchanged; a valid request is equivalent to calling"; "When the `seen_revision` of `confirm` is not a number, the request is dropped"
DST integration item 8: "for `open`, the server uses `target_userid` to look up the other party in `AllPlayers`"
clauses.note: A headless server has no connected players, so AllPlayers is empty; only the handler's existence is asserted.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 9: "listen for the world event `ms_playerleft` and call `self:OnPlayerLeft(player)` in the callback"
clauses.note: The listener's existence is observed (its removal lowers the world's ms_playerleft callback count); the event itself is never pushed because ~40 base-game listeners would receive a fake player, so the delegation is regex-only.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 9: "use `DoPeriodicTask` to periodically call the core `tick(self:Now())`"
clauses.note: The task's existence is observed through TheWorld.pendingtasks; that it calls tick cannot be seen by a synchronous suite.

clauses.anchor: DST integration item 9: "`OnRemoveFromEntity` must `RemoveEventCallback` with the same function object and `Cancel()` the periodic task"; "again; the component must be able to attach normally again"
DST integration item 10: "must not print to the log any line containing the words `error`, `failed` or `missing`; it must not leave `TODO`, `IMPLEMENT ME` or placeholder implementations"
clauses.note: Log lines naming the mod with those words make the evaluator fail the whole server run; TODO / IMPLEMENT ME are none_of patterns.

clauses.anchor: Base-game API contract, last paragraph: "The component uses the base-game `Class` form and hooks into the lifecycle with" OnSave / OnLoad / OnRemoveFromEntity
clauses.note: Methods are called with a receiver by the suite; the Class form itself is only implied by require-able component loading.
